High-frequency linear transducer (7.5–15 MHz) gray-scale and power/color Doppler sonography of the anterior, superior, lateral, and posterior compartments of the shoulder performed in longitudinal and transverse planes with dynamic maneuvers.
Located normally within the bicipital groove with intact overlying transverse humeral ligament. Normal uniform fibrillar echotexture without tenosynovitis, tendinosis, subluxation, or rupture.
Subscapularis Tendon: Normal fibrillar architecture and thickness with intact insertion onto the lesser tuberosity. No tear or calcific deposit.

Supraspinatus Tendon: Uniform fibrillar echotexture and normal thickness (5–7 mm) from the critical zone to the greater tuberosity footprint. No partial-thickness tear, full-thickness tear, or cortical irregularity.
Infraspinatus & Teres Minor Tendons: Normal fibrillar echotexture and intact insertions onto the posterior greater tuberosity without atrophy or tear.
Subacromial-Subdeltoid (SASD) Bursa: Normal collapsed appearance (less than 2 mm thick) without fluid distension, synovial thickening, or bursitis.
Posterior Glenohumeral Joint Recess & Spinoglenoid Notch: No significant joint effusion, labral cyst, or paralabral ganglion.
Acromioclavicular (AC) Joint: Normal joint space alignment (less than 5 mm) without capsular distension, osteophytes, or widening on cross-arm adduction.
Dynamic Abduction Evaluation: Smooth gliding of the supraspinatus tendon and SASD bursa beneath the coracoacromial arch without subacromial bunching or impingement.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Mild generalized right shoulder discomfort; rule out rotator cuff tear.

subs.title: Findings
items: High-frequency sonographic evaluation of the right shoulder demonstrates the long head of the biceps tendon normally seated within the bicipital groove with no surrounding sheath fluid.
The subscapularis, supraspinatus, infraspinatus, and teres minor tendons exhibit uniform, intact fibrillar architecture without tendinosis, calcifications, or partial/full-thickness tearing.
The subacromial-subdeltoid bursa is collapsed without fluid distension.
The acromioclavicular joint is normally aligned, and dynamic abduction shows smooth subacromial gliding without impingement.

subs.title: Impression
items: Normal right shoulder ultrasound. No evidence of rotator cuff tear, biceps tenosynovitis, bursitis, or subacromial impingement.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute severe right shoulder pain and inability to abduct arm following a fall onto an outstretched hand.

subs.title: Findings
items: Supraspinatus Tendon: There is a complete, full-thickness focal discontinuity involving the anterior-to-mid fibers of the supraspinatus tendon at the greater tuberosity footprint, measuring 1.6 cm in width (AP) with 1.4 cm of medial tendon retraction. The tendon defect is filled with hypoechoic fluid/hematoma, resulting in direct communication between the glenohumeral joint and the subacromial-subdeltoid bursa, with flattening of the overlying deltoid muscle contour ("sagging peribursal fat sign") and bare exposed greater tuberosity cartilage ("cartilage interface sign").
Bursa: Moderate complex fluid distending the subacromial-subdeltoid bursa.
Other Tendons: Subscapularis, infraspinatus, and biceps tendons are intact.

subs.title: Impression
items: Acute full-thickness tear of the right supraspinatus tendon (1.6 cm width x 1.4 cm retraction) with secondary subacromial-subdeltoid bursal effusion.
Orthopedic surgical consultation recommended.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Direct impact to the top of the left shoulder during cycling with focal superior shoulder pain and deformity.

subs.title: Findings
items: AC Joint: There is marked widening of the left acromioclavicular joint space measuring 11.5 mm (compared to 4.2 mm on the asymptomatic right side), accompanied by superior displacement (step-off deformity) of the distal clavicle relative to the acromion by 6 mm.

Ligaments & Capsule: Complete disruption of the superior acromioclavicular ligament and joint capsule with a localized 1.8 x 0.9 cm hypoechoic hematoma/effusion distending the joint space. Dynamic cross-arm adduction confirms gross AC joint instability.

subs.title: Impression
items: Acute high-grade (Rockwood Type III) separation/dislocation of the left acromioclavicular joint with dynamic instability and capsular disruption.
Correlate with bilateral weighted/unweighted Zanca view radiographs and orthopedic evaluation.

bank.title: 4. Traumatic Biceps Tendon Rupture ("Popeye" Deformity) & Medial Dislocation (Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute anterior shoulder pain and visible mid-arm bulge after heavy lifting.

subs.title: Findings
items: Empty Groove Pattern (Rupture): The intra-articular and bicipital groove segments of the left long head of the biceps tendon are absent ("empty bicipital groove sign"), replaced by hypoechoic fluid/hematoma. Scanning distally in the anterior arm reveals the retracted, coiled, bulbous tendon stump at the mid-humeral level surrounded by a 3.2 cm hematoma.
[Alternative: Medial Dislocation]: The long head of the biceps tendon is dislocated medially out of the empty bicipital groove, resting anterior to/within a torn subscapularis tendon insertion.

subs.title: Impression
items: Complete rupture and distal retraction of the left long head of the biceps tendon ("empty bicipital groove") with an associated mid-arm hematoma.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Painful arc of abduction (60°–120°) and night pain in the right shoulder.

subs.title: Findings
items: SASD Bursa: The right subacromial-subdeltoid bursa is distended by anechoic fluid and thickened, hypoechoic synovium (measuring 5.2 mm in combined thickness) with increased peripheral power Doppler hyperemia.
Supraspinatus Tendon: Mild diffuse tendinosis (thickened to 7.8 mm with heterogeneous hypoechogenicity) without partial or full-thickness tear.

Dynamic Maneuver: During active/passive shoulder abduction, there is visible bunching and pooling of bursal fluid and the thickened supraspinatus tendon against the lateral edge of the acromion, reproducing the patient's pain.

subs.title: Impression
items: Right subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis with mild supraspinatus tendinosis and positive dynamic subacromial impingement.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Severe, acute-on-chronic atraumatic lateral shoulder pain with restricted range of motion.

subs.title: Findings
items: Within the distal substance of the right supraspinatus tendon, approximately 1.0 cm proximal to the greater tuberosity insertion, there is a well-defined, ovoid hyperechoic calcific deposit measuring 1.3 x 0.6 cm demonstrating faint/incomplete posterior acoustic shadowing ("slurry/resorptive phase" appearance).
Surrounding the calcification, the tendon is swollen and hypoechoic with marked focal hyperemia on power Doppler and mild reactive fluid in the overlying subacromial-subdeltoid bursa.

subs.title: Impression
items: Acute-phase (resorptive) calcific tendinopathy of the right supraspinatus tendon (1.3 cm deposit) with marked pericalcific hyperemia and mild reactive subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis.
Patient is a candidate for ultrasound-guided barbotage (lavage/aspiration) and corticosteroid injection if conservative measures fail.

bank.title: 7. Partial-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tear (Articular vs. Bursal-Sided) (Non-Traumatic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Chronic overhead athlete shoulder pain; rule out cuff tear.

subs.title: Findings
items: Articular-Sided Partial Tear (PASTA): Along the deep articular surface of the distal right supraspinatus tendon at the footprint, there is a well-defined, focal hypoechoic/anechoic defect measuring 7 x 4 mm involving approximately 40% of the tendon thickness, accompanied by focal cortical pitting/irregularity of the underlying greater tuberosity. The superficial bursal fibers remain intact and smooth without deltoid sagging.
[Alternative Bursal-Sided]: Focal anechoic defect along the superficial bursal surface of the supraspinatus tendon communicating with a mildly distended SASD bursa, with intact deep articular fibers.

subs.title: Impression
items: Partial-thickness articular-sided tear (PASTA lesion) of the distal right supraspinatus tendon involving less than 50% of tendon thickness, with underlying greater tuberosity cortical irregularity.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Progressive severe stiffness and global loss of active and passive external rotation in a diabetic patient.

subs.title: Findings
items: Rotator Interval & CHL: Marked thickening and hypoechogenicity of the coracohumeral ligament (CHL) measuring 4.2 mm (normal less than 3 mm) and hypoechoic vascularized soft-tissue thickening within the rotator interval, demonstrating Grade 2 hyperemia on power Doppler.
Axillary Pouch: Thickening of the inferior glenohumeral capsule at the axillary recess (measuring 4.8 mm; normal less than 3.5 mm).

Biceps Tendon Sheath: Moderate anechoic fluid distending the long head of the biceps tendon sheath with synovial hypertrophy, while the rotator cuff tendons remain intact. Dynamic external rotation is markedly restricted.

subs.title: Impression
items: Sonographic findings consistent with adhesive capsulitis ("frozen shoulder"), evidenced by coracohumeral ligament thickening (4.2 mm), hypervascular rotator interval synovitis, axillary pouch thickening, and restricted dynamic external rotation.
